title: JUSINOVA v. NORTH MACEDONIA
summary: In the case of Jusinova v. North Macedonia, the applicant, Ms. Mizafer Jusinova, was represented by the European Roma Rights Centre and is identified in the case materials as a member of the Roma community. The application concerned a serious incident involving the right to life, protected under Article 2 of the European Convention on Human Rights. While the judgment does not detail the underlying events, the involvement of the European Roma Rights Centre and the reference to Article 2 suggest the case related to a life-threatening situation or loss of life affecting a Roma individual. The application was lodged in December 2018, and both parties subsequently reached a friendly settlement. Under this agreement, the Government of North Macedonia undertook to pay Ms. Jusinova €12,000 in compensation for pecuniary and non-pecuniary damage, as well as costs and expenses. The European Court of Human Rights was satisfied that the settlement respected the principles of the Convention and, accordingly, struck the case out of its list under Article 39. No findings of a violation were made, as the case was resolved amicably before a full judgment on the merits.
